text:
sam: Heads up — customer ACME reported credit balance not updated after a series of short-lived sessions. looks like tokens were consumed but the invoice shows zero for that window :confused:

lina: which pipeline do we think missed the events? routing proxy -> ingress -> metering-transform -> events-queue -> billing-job, right? :thinking_face:

mike: yes. quick hypothesis: during last night's rollout of the routing change, some sessions were routed to the new proxy which replies 202 while we were still expecting sync metering. could be 'orphaned' requests that never hit the metering-transform.

jess: can you paste an example request_id? I can correlate in logs/BigQuery.

sam: pasted below — found in proxy logs but no corresponding metering_event.

```
proxy.log: 2024-11-22T03:12:11Z request_id=0f7a-9c3e route=new-routing-v2 session_id=sess-84 user=acme-org model=gpt-open-13k tokens=142
ingress.log: 2024-11-22T03:12:11Z request_id=0f7a-9c3e accepted vendor=proxy-v2
# no metering-transform entry for request_id 0f7a-9c3e
```

oliver: that's the exact pattern I saw in the canary window. the routing change returns early 202 to the client and writes a lightweight ack_event, then does async handoff. if the handoff fails or timeouts we drop the token accounting call.

pranav: hmm our SLA for at-least-once metering is broken then. we rely on ingress to push to transform, which async-retries to events-queue. need to check backpressure and retry policy.

lina: timeline: rollout at 03:08 -> spike in transient 5xx to transform between 03:11-03:15 -> many 202s from proxy. sounds like backpressure + new routing semantics.

billing-bot: Automated alert: invoice-discrepancy detected for customer acme-org. suspect_missing_events=23 window=2024-11-22T03:00:00Z-2024-11-22T04:00:00Z

mike: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) pause new-routing-v2 rollout (canary -> stop) 2) re-ingest proxy ack_event stream with reshaping logic to reconstruct missing metering events 3) fallback to pre-rollout routing for sessions with >100 tokens until resolved.

jess: I can kick off a re-ingest job if we can produce a complete ack_event export. does proxy persist ack_event to s3 or only ephemeral?

sam: proxy persists ack to kafka topic ack_events_v2 and we have retention 48h. re-ingest should be possible. downside: ack events sometimes lack token breakdown, only total_count. need transformation heuristics.

qa-bot: Quick triage test checklist: reproduce under canary with delayed transform, verify re-ingest produces same metering_event shape, ensure invoices update in staging.

pranav: note on heuristics — don't infer model-level token split from total_count (we'll get incorrect per-model billing). prefer creating 'reconciliation credit' entries with metadata: source=ack_reingest, reason=orphaned_handoff, original_request_ids=[...]. That way billing can accept a credit rather than attempt exact reconstruction.

lina: agree — plumb a reconciliation event type into billing pipeline so finance can review. Add UI flag in console to accept auto-credits for severe gaps. UX: show count, sample request_ids, rationale.

mike: +1. also will add metric: ack_events_without_metering / total_ack_events and alert at 0.1% with pager.

sam: action items: mike pause rollout (in progress), jess export ack_events_v2 (assigned), oliver validate retry loops and increase transform retry to 5 with exponential backoff, pranav draft reconciliation event schema, lina track console UX change request. I'll open a follow-up in #incidents for billing reconciliation.

oliver: paused rollout confirmed. :white_check_mark:

jess: export started (topic -> s3), ETA ~20m.

pranav: I'll sketch schema and post a PR for the billing team to review.

sam: thanks all. let's aim to re-ingest to staging and run invoice pipeline before unpausing. ping me if you find additional weirdness. :thumbsup:
